3.  24-53164  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Data Overview
  Presentation from Dalton Dorr.

  Dalton Dorr, Homeless Services Bureau Data Analyst, presented in person.
  • The presentation began with a summary of the last quarter's MSC activities.
  He explained that since it is difficult to track the number of participants and/or
  participants through the system because of the variety of externalities and
  outcome lags that come with that type of data, the best metrics to use to
  measure results are services.
  • Demand is easier to identify at the MSC versus supply because there are
  other factors to consider with supply.
  • Commissioners and City Staff discussed shelter beds in the City and the
  demand for Shelter beds.
  • City staff Dalton Dorr continued to present his presentation to discuss the
  inactivity policy.
  • Commissioner Lewis suggested Commissioners when asking staff for more
  data, explain the context and specifics of what they hope to use the data for.
  This will help staff provide accurate information.
  • Commissioners had questions about case management, the HOP, and how
  individuals are notified of available beds and what are the eligibility
  requirements.
  • City staff responded, individuals that who go to the MSC looking for
  assistance are connected with a case manager, when a housing/bed
  connection is made, case managers reach out through various avenues
  phone calls, emails, and using outreach workers to go to their last known
  place of contact. There are also different types of programming for housing
  with different criteria however, the City of Long Beach is a housing-first
  jurisdiction and does not screen out for substance use.
  • Commissioners continued discussion regarding meeting the demand for
  services and requesting more details data.
  • City staff added, that meeting the demand when it comes to case
  management and other services is difficult because there are not enough
  resources. Leadership often has to chose where to split their limited
  resources, for example, hiring more case managers would not solve the
  referral process if there are no locations to refer in.
  • Other services are sometimes more difficult or just impossible to track, like
  meals. Daily, 30-40 meals are served at MSC during lunch. Services
  rendered by the substance use coordinators are tracked using another
  system since HMIS is not HIPAA compliant.
  • Commissioner Chotiswatdi agreed with the staff sentiment of limited
  resources, as in her line of work the housing navigators she works with are
  unable to find shelter to place people.

  Page 3 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, MAY 1, 2024

  BILLIE JEAN KING LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  • With the new Coordinated Entry integration into HMIS, staff’s goal is to be
  more transparent with everyone using the system. There is still data that
  needs to be collected and cleaned up since this system is fairly new.
  • Commissioners spoke on the interest of learning what the gap
  between resources and availability. Commissioners pointed out that even
  though resources may be available there are some individuals that will turn
  away services and availability because they don’t want the housing. There
  are individuals that are comfortable living on the streets and it can be hard to
  replace that with shelter.
  • Commisoners had questions regarding the overlapping of services within
  jurisdictions and mental/medical health.
  • Staff responded that to be connected to services a person must go to the
  MSC, MAC, or another access center in the CES. Working with individuals
  who require mental and medical health is challenging since those resources
  are even more limited. However, our staff does their best to create those
  connections and ensure that pathways out of medical care are met with case
  management.
  • City staff Dalton Dorr will work to provide quarterly data reports starting July
  as a report back to the committee.
  • Public Comment from Karen was heard, she thanked the staff for the
  presentation, however, she believes that there is a lot of information that
  might not be captured. She will be on the panel with the Secretary of
  Medicare and asked to connect with City staff on data that she can use to
  share during her meeting with the Secretary.

  • Announced staff promotions, and ongoing recruitment for various positions.
  As well as 15 position postings coming soon.
  • Next week on May 8th at 11 am the PIT Count data and report will be
  released.
  • The property at 4151 Fountain St. has been cleared to demolish the building
  and start working on the affordable housing project. 72 apartments for low-
  income families and people with disabilities will be constructed, the
  developer will be Linc Housing.
  • Johnson v Grant Pass, this was an offshoot of Martin V. Boise an ordinance
  that banned activities around sleeping in public right away. Federal leaders
  and City leaders are awaiting the June ruling as it might change how the
  surrounding jurisdictions enforce activities of unsheltered homelessness.
